DEMOLITION OF AN EXISITNG POOL FOR A SINGLE FAMILY AS PER CODE BULLETIN : No. B-0403

The following conditions apply to the demolition of floor slabs from in-ground swimming pools:
1. A building permit is required for the demolition.
2. The floor slab must be broken up so that the rubble is no larger than 1-foot in diameter,
allowing drainage into the ground.
3. Loose re-bar must be removed from the hole. Embedded re-bar may remain. Clean
fill must be placed into the cavity.
4. An inspection must be conducted before the cavity is backfilled to verify that the slab
has been demolished properly and that the loose re-bar has been removed.

properties.description:
For the demolition of an in-ground swimming pool.
1. A building permit is required for the demolition.
2. The floor slab must be broken up so that the rubble is no larger than 1-foot in diameter, allowing for drainage into the ground.
3. Loose re-bar must be removed from the hole. Embedded re-bar may remain. Clean fill must be placed into the cavity.
4. An inspection must be conducted before the cavity is backfilled to verify that the slab has been demolished properly and that the loose re-bar has been removed. 
NOTE: Although not a requirement, the Department recommends that side walls of the swimming pool also be removed. Under no circumstance shall the walls remain functioning as retaining walls.

1. A building permit is required for the demolition.
2. The floor slab must be broken up so that the rubble is no larger than 1-foot in diameter,
allowing drainage into the ground.
3. Loose re-bar must be removed from the hole. Embedded re-bar may remain. Clean
fill must be placed into the cavity.
4. An inspection must be conducted before the cavity is backfilled to verify that the slab
has been demolished properly and that the loose re-bar has been removed.

NOTE: Although not a requirement, the Department recommends that the side walls of the swimming pool also be removed. Under no circumstance shall the walls remain functioning as retaining walls

furnish & wire one 22kw Air Cooled Honeywell/Generac Electric Generator powered by liquid propane/natural gas operated engine. The 22kW generator will provide a 91.67 Amp rating for the total load setting. Install one Honeywell/Generac 200 Amp automatic transfer switch outside to the right of the 200amp meter socket. All branch circuits connected to the electrical panel will be transferred to the generator during the power outage condition and will have power availability simultaneously for the contents of the load center. The transfer switch will redirect all of the desired circuitry to the generator during a power outage condition.  This equipment will be located outside or wherever application is able to be installed to meet all the current electrical codes. Circuitry will not be transferred to the generator during the weekly exercise period, only during a power outage. Installation of the control wiring and connection points between the transfer switch and the generator equipment. This wiring will be installed for the equipment monitoring, automatic engine start function, exercise routine, power failure-alert, run time monitoring and battery charging equipment. This wiring will be routed from transfer switch outside through the entire length of the crawl space and trenched 25 to 30 feet over  to the location to the generator that will be 2ft off the bock of the pool house. All work to the 2014 NEC and with
